fields.meta_title: Sports Quiz: Play 8 Questions, Then Build One | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take an 8-question sports quiz with a source behind every answer, then build your own for your league or a ballpark crowd.
fields.h1: Build a Sports Quiz That Scores Every Player
fields.hero_description: Build a sports quiz for your league or class that scores each player and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Sports Quiz Built With Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Emergent writes the questions and the scoring from your prompt. The app saves each answer to a table sorted by player or question.
fields.feature_1:
Questions pitched at the players you name

Name the sport, the level, and the rule set, such as U12 soccer or seventh-grade volleyball, and Emergent drafts multiple-choice questions to match. Edit any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Scores saved by player and question

Every answer is a row in a database you own: the player, the question, the option picked, and whether it was right. Sort by question to find the one that stumped the most players.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Players see one question per screen with a progress bar, so a fan in the bleachers or a referee on the sideline finishes on a phone. Emergent puts no cap on how many players answer.
fields.feature_4:
A pass mark that sends an email

Set a pass mark, such as 10 of 12, and the app emails the organizer the name of each player who falls below it. Point the alert at a Slack channel when a whole league needs it.
fields.feature_5:
Leaderboards that add up a season

Ask for a leaderboard and the app totals each player's scores week by week. Change the scoring, add a bonus round, or reset the table for a new season with one more prompt.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and the code on paid plans

Run the quiz on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and bring it back next season.

fields.tab_content_1:
Referees who score under 10 of 12 get a clinic invite

Wickliffe Youth Soccer sends a 12-question laws quiz to its 26 volunteer referees before the fall season, and each score is saved under the referee's name. The 7 who scored under 10 of 12 got an email inviting them to the Saturday clinic. The other 19 are cleared for opening weekend.
fields.tab_content_2:
Lesson one is rotation, the question 49 of 84 missed

Before the volleyball unit, Dellwood Middle School's 3 seventh-grade PE classes, 84 students in all, take a 10-question quiz on class tablets. Each answer is saved with the student and the class period. The rotation question was missed by 49 of 84, more than any other, so the first lesson starts on the court with rotation.
fields.tab_content_3:
Dana Kasprzak in first with 38 points after week 9

Every Monday at Lorimer Freight, the 12 people in the office fantasy football league answer 5 questions on the weekend's games. The app adds each score to a season total and posts the standings to the league's Slack channel. After week 9, Dana Kasprzak is in first with 38 points, 2 ahead of Theo Akande.
fields.tab_content_4:
With 612 perfect scores, one seat is drawn

Between innings, the Coalport Riverhawks put a QR code on the scoreboard that opens a 3-question fan quiz. On Friday night, 1,120 fans answered on their phones, and 612 got all 3 right. The app drew one seat from those 612, and section 108, row F, seat 4 won a signed bat.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Sports Quiz Players Finish
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run a sports quiz with fair questions, a pass mark or standings, and a table of what players missed.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick one sport or mix them
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Show a source under each answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the players before you write a question: volunteer referees, a seventh-grade class, an office league, or fans in the stands. Each group needs a different level, and putting it in your prompt lets Emergent pitch the questions to match.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A rules check works best on one sport and one rule book. A trivia round can mix sports, but keep each question to one fact a player could look up. Say which kind you want and how many questions it should have.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give every question four options of the same kind and length, such as four years or four team names. One silly option turns a question into a free point. Ask Emergent to redraft any option set that gives the answer away.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a one-line explanation under each answer that says where the fact comes from. A source settles a dispute before it starts. The quiz at the top of this page follows the pattern, with a source behind all 8 answers.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose a pass mark or standings
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide what the score is for. A rules check needs a pass mark and a list of who fell below it. A weekly game needs a running total per player and standings the whole group can see after each round.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, have three people take the quiz on their phones. Rewrite any question that two of them read differently. Then open the table and check that each answer saved as its own row with the right score beside it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the round, sort the answers by question. The one most players missed becomes the next lesson, the clinic topic, or next week's bonus question. Change the quiz by prompt and send the next round to the same players.

faq_plan.q: What is a good sports quiz question?
faq_plan.ref: What is a good sports quiz question?

prov.original: What is a good sports quiz question?

faq_plan.a: A good sports quiz question has one answer a player can check and four options that all sound right to someone who half-knows it. Pitch it at the people playing: a rules question for referees, a stats question for a fantasy league. Skip trick wording: the quiz should test what players know, not how closely they read.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a sports quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe the quiz in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the sport, who plays, and how many questions. Say what the score should do, such as set a pass mark or feed a season leaderboard. Emergent builds the questions and the scoring, with a database behind them. Play it yourself, change any question by prompt, then share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is my best sport quiz?
faq_plan.ref: What is my best sport quiz?

prov.original: What is my best sport quiz?

faq_plan.a: A best-sport quiz is a matching quiz: each answer points toward a sport, and the result names the one your answers lean toward. Ask about team or solo play, indoors or outdoors, and contact or none. Emergent can build that matching quiz from a prompt and save each taker's result to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What are some good sports quiz questions and answers for 2026?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good sports quiz questions and answers for 2026?

prov.original: What are some good sports quiz questions and answers for 2026?

faq_plan.a: Good 2026 questions come from the year's biggest events. How many teams played in the 2026 FIFA World Cup? 48, the first edition that size. How many countries hosted it? Three, another first. Which host became the first country to stage the World Cup three times? Mexico. Keep a source beside each of your sports quiz questions and answers.

faq_plan.q: Can you give me some examples of sports quiz questions?
faq_plan.ref: Can you give me some examples of sports quiz questions?

prov.original: Can you give me some examples of sports quiz questions?

faq_plan.a: Yes. Here are two sports quiz questions with their answers. In a soccer match, what is the most players a team can have on the field? Eleven, one of them the goalkeeper. What is the highest possible score in a game of bowling? 300. The playable quiz on this page has 6 more, each with its source.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free sports quiz for my team or class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Build a free sports quiz for your team or class and share the link. Every answer lands in a database you own, with no cap on responses.

faq_plan.q: How do I write a guess-the-athlete sports quiz?
faq_plan.hint: Who am i sports quiz questions?
faq_plan.a: Write three clues per athlete, hardest first: a career stat, then a former team, then a nickname. Score 3 points for a correct guess after the first clue, 2 after the second, and 1 after the third. Put the clues and the point values in your prompt, and the app reveals one clue at a time.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a sports quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Match the length to the moment: 3 questions for fans between innings, 5 for a weekly league game, and 12 for a rules check with a pass mark. Past 12, split a longer quiz into rounds that players can finish in one sitting on a phone.

faq_plan.q: Can players answer a sports quiz in groups and share one score?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for group scoring in your prompt: each group enters its name once, every answer is saved under that name, and the app ranks the groups when the round closes. It suits a booster club fundraiser where each table plays together.

faq_plan.q: Can I add a time limit to each sports quiz question?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for a timer in your prompt, such as 20 seconds per question, and the app moves to the next question when it runs out and saves that one as unanswered. With the clock on screen, nobody argues about whether a late answer counted.

quiz.title: Sports Quiz: 8 Questions From the Field to the Lanes
quiz.intro: Eight questions across soccer, basketball, baseball, tennis, bowling, golf, the Olympics, and hockey. Every answer comes with its source.

questions.text: In a soccer match, what is the most players each team can have on the field?
questions.explanation: Each side fields up to eleven players, and one of them must be the goalkeeper.

source.quote: A match is played by two teams, each with a maximum of eleven players; one must be the goalkeeper

questions.text: In basketball, a field goal made from behind the arc is worth how many points?
questions.explanation: A field goal is worth two points, or three when the shooter is behind the three-point line.

source.quote: A field goal is worth two points, unless made from behind the three-point line, when it is worth three

questions.text: How many innings make up a regulation game in Major League Baseball?
questions.explanation: Each inning has six outs, three for each team, and a regulation game runs nine innings.

source.quote: A full inning consists of six outs, three for each team, and, in Major League Baseball and most other adult leagues, a regulation game consists of nine innings

questions.text: In tennis scoring, what does the word love mean?
questions.explanation: A player with no games won in a set is said to have love.

source.quote: the state of having won zero games is called "love"

questions.text: What is the highest possible score in one game of bowling?
questions.explanation: A perfect game takes 12 strikes in a row.

source.quote: The highest possible score for a game is 300, achieved by rolling 12 consecutive strikes

questions.text: St Andrews set the standard length of a golf course in 1764. How many holes?
questions.explanation: Members at St Andrews cut their course from 22 holes to 18 in 1764.

source.quote: In 1764, the standard 18-hole golf course was created at St Andrews when members modified the course from 22 to 18 holes

questions.text: How many interlocking rings make up the Olympic symbol?
questions.explanation: Count them on any Olympic flag: five rings, linked together.

source.quote: The Olympic rings consist of five interlocking rings

questions.text: In ice hockey, what is a hat trick?

options.text: Three goals in a single game

questions.explanation: The same term covers field hockey and bandy.

source.quote: In field hockey, ice hockey, and bandy, a hat trick occurs when a player scores three goals in a single game

results.title: Still Warming Up
results.description: You got 3 or fewer right. Read the answers below, then play again: the rules questions get easier once you have seen them once. A quiz like this one, built for your club or class, saves every answer so you can see which questions tripped people up.

results.title: Starting Lineup
results.description: You got 4 to 6 right, enough to hold your own at a sports bar trivia night. Check the explanations for the ones you missed. Build your own version and send it to your league to see who knows more.

results.title: All-Star
results.description: You got 7 or 8 right. You know your rules and your records. Turn that into a quiz of your own for your league, your team, or your class, with a leaderboard that keeps score every week.

plan.angle: The top 10 is all quizzes to play: Sporcle, JetPunk, Yardbarker, the BBC, the Guardian, Britannica and HowStuffWorks host their own sports trivia, and Brainpower and SignUpGenius publish question lists to copy. None shows how to run a sports quiz as your own app, with your own questions, scores saved by player, and a list of what people missed. This page gives the searcher both: an 8-question sports quiz to play on the page, every answer sourced, then four sports quizzes a youth soccer club, a middle school gym class, an office fantasy league and a minor league ballpark run as their own app, each saving answers to a table they own.
